{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"4a8174a45f7c1dcbb63097d4400f5178e197d6532e8bc16cb07cc7258135d56f","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:91","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Hearing requests, vehicle emergencies, brake and steering failures, avoiding rear-end and head-on crashes, compromising between risks, skids, road debris and animals","heading":"C — Requesting an MVD hearing on time, tire blowouts, vehicle fires, overheating, power steering, headlight and brake failure, avoiding rear-end and head-on crashes, seat belts, compromising between hazards, skid recovery, road debris and animals on the road","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Requesting an MVD hearing on time, tire blowouts, vehicle fires, overheating, power steering, headlight and brake failure, avoiding rear-end and head-on crashes, seat belts, compromising between hazards, skid recovery, road debris and animals on the road
Knowledge domain: why a hearing request must be filed on time, how to handle a tire blowout, a vehicle fire and an overheating engine, what to do when power steering, headlights or brakes fail, how to reduce the harm of a rear-end or head-on crash, how to split space between two hazards, how to steer out of a skid, and how to deal with debris and animals on Arizona roads.

FACT_ID: sec21-F01 | anchor: A01
File any hearing request within the time the law allows, because you may lose your right to a hearing if you delay. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F02 | anchor: A01
The Executive Hearing Office may give only general information, so for specific legal advice you might consult an attorney. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F03 | anchor: A01
Skids, tire blowouts and mechanical failures can happen at any time, so be prepared to handle them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F04 | anchor: A01
Checking your tire pressure regularly lowers your chances of a blowout. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F05 | anchor: A01
If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle traveling straight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F06 | anchor: A01
During a blowout, ease off the gas pedal and do not use the brakes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F07 | anchor: A01
After a blowout, let the vehicle slow until it is almost stopped, then signal, pull off the roadway and brake. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F08 | anchor: A01
Vehicle fires are usually caused by a short circuit in the electrical system. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F09 | anchor: A01
If your vehicle catches fire, pull off the road quickly, shut off the ignition to cut electrical power, get every passenger away from the car and call 911. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F10 | anchor: A01
Always carry a fire extinguisher, and an ABC-rated dry chemical extinguisher is best for vehicle fires. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F11 | anchor: A01
Never use water on burning gasoline, because water spreads the flames. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F12 | anchor: A01
Without an extinguisher, a heavy blanket, a heavy coat or sand can help smother the flames. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F13 | anchor: A01
If there is any sign the fire may be beyond your control, get away from the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F14 | anchor: A01
Steam rising from under the hood may mean the cooling system has overheated. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F15 | anchor: A01
If the engine overheats, pull to the side of the road and shut off the engine right away. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F16 | anchor: A01
With an overheated engine, raise the hood but leave the radiator cap closed, since opening it while hot can release steam and cause severe burns. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F17 | anchor: A01
Carry extra water for the radiator, and add it only after the engine has cooled. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-F18 | anchor: A02
If power steering fails, for example when the engine dies in a turn, grip the wheel firmly with both hands to finish the turn and move to the right side of the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F19 | anchor: A02
After a power steering failure, stop the car, pressing extra hard on the brake pedal if the vehicle has power brakes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F20 | anchor: A02
If your headlights fail, first try the high and low beam switch, which may bring them back. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F21 | anchor: A02
If the headlights stay off, turn the headlight switch on and off several times. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F22 | anchor: A02
If the headlights still fail, switch on the parking lights, emergency flashers or turn signals, then pull to the side of the road and stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F23 | anchor: A02
Many vehicles have anti-lock braking systems (ABS), and anti-lock brakes should not be pumped. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F24 | anchor: A02
If brakes fail on a vehicle without anti-lock brakes, pump the pedal rapidly, which may build enough pressure to stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F25 | anchor: A02
If pumping does not help, apply the parking brake slowly while holding the brake release so you can ease off if the rear wheels lock and the car starts to skid. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F26 | anchor: A02
During a brake failure, shift to a lower gear and look for a safe place to stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F27 | anchor: A02
If you are stopped at a light or stop sign and a vehicle is coming up fast behind you, pull forward if you can to give it more room to stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F28 | anchor: A02
If a rear-end crash cannot be avoided, brace yourself between the steering wheel and the seat back and release the brake an instant before impact. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F29 | anchor: A02
To head off a possible head-on crash, slow down, flash your headlights and sound your horn to warn the other driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F30 | anchor: A02
Facing a possible head-on crash, head for the shoulder and get off the road away from the oncoming driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F31 | anchor: A02
If a head-on crash cannot be avoided, steer so as to make the impact less severe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F32 | anchor: A02
Buckling your safety belt every time is your single best protection against injury if a crash happens. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-F33 | anchor: A03
Compromise means that when two or more risks cannot be separated, you give the most room to the greatest or most likely danger. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F34 | anchor: A03
With oncoming cars on your left and a child on a bike on your right, the child is the most likely to move suddenly, so moving closer to the center line is the right compromise. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F35 | anchor: A03
A slippery road or braking too sharply can throw your vehicle into a skid. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F36 | anchor: A03
In a skid, stop pressing the brake, since more braking only makes the skid worse. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F37 | anchor: A03
In a skid, quickly turn the wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go, which is the direction of the skid. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F38 | anchor: A03
As the car starts to straighten, quickly turn the wheel back the other way, and keep correcting until the vehicle returns to its normal path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F39 | anchor: A03
Road debris is common in Arizona, including pieces of blown tires, unsecured loads falling off trucks and rocks washed onto the road in storms. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F40 | anchor: A03
A common debris crash happens when a driver swerves to miss the debris, loses control and leaves the road, when driving over it might have been far less severe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F41 | anchor: A03
Stay alert and think ahead about what you would do if debris suddenly appeared in front of you, since you may have only a split second to decide. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F42 | anchor: A03
Wildlife may dart onto the road in unexpected places, and livestock may get out when people leave gates open or cut fences. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F43 | anchor: A03
When an animal is in the roadway, brake down to the lowest speed you safely can and steer to avoid a direct hit without losing control. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F44 | anchor: A03
If an animal is near but not yet on the road, do not honk, because the noise may startle it into your path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-F45 | anchor: A03
Report an animal that endangers traffic by calling 911 so law enforcement can respond. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

Misconceptions: braking hard during a blowout or a skid makes things worse; anti-lock brakes should not be pumped, while ordinary brakes that fail should be; water must never be thrown on a gasoline fire; swerving hard around debris can be more dangerous than driving over it; honking at an animal beside the road can drive it into your path.
Mnemonics: Blowout, hold straight and coast; skid, steer where you want to go; overheating, hood up, cap on.
Glossary: blowout means a sudden tire failure; ABS means an anti-lock braking system that keeps wheels from locking; ABC-rated extinguisher means one rated for common, liquid and electrical fires; compromise means splitting space so the biggest or most likely danger gets the most room; skid means losing tire grip so the vehicle slides.
Dynamic facts: hearing request deadlines are set by law and the Executive Hearing Office procedures and contact details can be revised by the issuer; the emergency steps themselves are general driving guidance.
